thread.title: Dow Dives 383 Points on a Bushel of Bad News

title: Dow Dives 383 Points on a Bushel of Bad News
text:
Dow Dives 383 Points on a Bushel of Bad News By Jan. 3, 2019 11:57 a.m. ET Order Reprints Michael Haddad Text size
Resolution Broken . All three indexes were lodged in the red Thursday: Positive momentum on the first trading day of 2019 was no match for a downbeat forecast from Apple (ticker: AAPL), and bad news kept coming. In today’s Intraday Update , we… look at the core worries around Apple; touch on manufacturing concerns; and see what’s sinking airlines.
Trouble Ahead, Trouble Behind
Stocks are suffering on Thursday, as Apple fueled the flames of slowing global growth concerns.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average is down 383.64 points, or 1.6%, to 22,962.60. The S&P 500 is off 1.3%, and the Nasdaq Composite is falling 1.5%. The stock market is sliding, interest rates are rising and trade tensions continue. What will the second two years of the Trump presidency look like economically? WSJ's Gerald F. Seib explains. Photos: Getty
Apple, which blamed slower iPhone sales, especially in China, for its reduced first-quarter forecast, is the big story of the day. Although it received some analyst support, price targets are coming down too, and the stock’s skid, which began after hours Wednesday following the announcement, has deepened, and spread to supplier as well.
Of course, Apple’s huge size means that a bad day for the company is often a bad day for the market. Yet the problem is compounded by the ongoing trade war: Apple’s latest announcement is only more fodder for fears that tariffs are putting the brakes on global growth.
The news is also especially unwelcome for those who hoped that this would be the year of a tech rebound. “Apple’s news was reminiscent of Facebook ’s (FB) massive disappointment of investors over the summer, which ended up forming a part of the decline in the FAANG stocks,” writes T.D. Ameritrade’s J.J. Kinahan. “One question for 2019 could be whether the FAANG stocks can mount a comeback.”
Apple may have grabbed the most headlines, but it wasn’t the only piece of bad news. Thursday morning also saw December’s ISM manufacturing index hit its lowest level since 2016—yet another blow for those looking for reassurances about the health of the global economy. Newsletter Sign-up
When taken in conjunction with other economic indicators, the ISM manufacturing index points to an environment that is not as robust as in recent quarters. That was widely expected; the degree of the slowdown was not,” writes Plante Moran Financial Advisors’ Jim Baird. “Even so, the manufacturing sector is still expanding and is far from recessionary territory.”
That may be of cold comfort today, however, with stocks tumbling. Yet, JPMorgan’s Jason Hunter argues that we might be nearing a capitulation point, as technical favor a short-term rebound, following the “important dividing line” crossed by last month’s selloff. “The extreme oversold conditions generated by the December breakdown and sharp decline have historically been associated with short-term bottoms and multi-week rebounds. Those signals also have the potential to mark the beginning of a more significant medium- to longer-term bottoming process, but we need to see more price action before we can put together a high conviction view.”
Conviction would be nice—although bears seem to have had the monopoly of it lately.
